# UNPACKED

> An interactive field guide that traces 19 everyday objects from an ordinary room — keyboard, lamp, office chair, mug, steel desk, window, book, ceiling fan, candle, armchair, steel bottle, earbuds, matcha whisk, LED strip, power bank, ball, blender, SSD and ballpoint pen — down their supply chains: every part, every machine, every material, to the mine, oil well, forest or quarry it came from. 210 processes, 223 links; four chains end in crude oil, three in iron ore, three in copper. Live at https://0xhzsa.github.io/unpacked/

Each object has a scroll-story chapter (first-person for parts and products,
third-person for machines, materials and sources), an appendix ledger of verified
specs and histories, and a whole-room graph where the 19 chains visibly merge over
shared machines, materials and mines. Photos are Wikimedia Commons (CC BY / CC BY-SA);
per-file credits live in the repo's RECOVERY-NOTE.md and a credit strip is on the home page.
Facts are sourced: manufacturer-published specs only (e.g. Thermos 24h cold / 12h hot),
widely reported figures kept attributable (Stanley $73M (2019) → $750M (2023)), and any
unverifiable number removed during an explicit fact-check pass.
